key_insight: Random, intermittent jet forcing mixes a two-layer stratified fluid while the interface can either rise and broaden or, at large density jumps, sharpen even as irreversible mixing occurs.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict transport and entrainment across density interfaces in geophysical and industrial stratified flows where forcing is unsteady and spatially heterogeneous.
method: Two-layer salt-stratified fluid experiments forced by a randomly actuated synthetic jet array (RASJA).
Interface evolution measured with the light attenuation technique.
Background potential energy used to assess irreversible mixing and compare regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that interface rise speed decreases with density jump and that both weak- and strong-jump cases show comparable irreversible energy changes despite different interface-shape evolution.
watch_item: Because the study is laboratory-based and uses a specific random jet forcing setup, direct transfer to fully natural flows or different forcing spectra may require caution.
paper_title: Mixing and sharpening at the interface of a two-layer fluid forced by random jets
